title: Overview
body:
## Overview

sheet-llm is a chat-driven music notation editor. Describe music in plain language and an AI composes and edits a real score, shown as standard staff notation.

The core loop is short: type a request in the prompt bar, the AI generates or edits the score, review the change, then refine with more requests or edit by hand. Two ways to change a score work side by side. Ask the AI in chat, or edit directly by clicking notes and using the floating menu, the keyboard, or the command palette.

Start a score three ways:

- A text prompt, such as `a short waltz in A minor`
- A blank score
- An imported file via **Import**. Supported formats: MusicXML, MIDI, ABC.

A finished score plays back with synthesized audio. It also exports to MIDI, PDF, and MusicXML. Work saves per session, and sessions are listed in the left sidebar.

Main entry points:

- The prompt bar at the bottom
- The command palette, **Cmd/Ctrl+K**
- The keyboard-shortcuts sheet, press **?**
- This guide

title: Composing with AI
body:
## Composing with AI

sheet-llm builds and edits scores from plain-language requests. The prompt bar sits at the bottom: type a request and press **Enter**, or click **Send**. On a blank or freshly imported score, suggestion chips appear; clicking one fills the prompt bar with a common request.

Requests fall into a few kinds:

| Goal | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Add bars at the end | `continue this` |
| Insert bars in the middle | `insert 2 bars after bar 4` |
| Rewrite a section | `replace bars 5-8 with a turnaround` |
| Tweak one bar | `add a sharp to the B in measure 4` |
| Start over | `compose a new piece` |
| Ask a question | `what key is this in?` |

Questions get a text answer and change nothing. The AI never silently overwrites bars it wasn't asked to touch; the server checks that untouched bars stay intact.

Small changes (4 or fewer notes) highlight in amber in place: press **Enter** to accept, **Esc** to reject. Larger changes open a proposal panel on the right; **Enter** accepts all, **Esc** rejects. Editing by hand while a proposal waits stashes it, and a toast at bottom-left offers about 30 seconds to restore it.

If a request would replace more than half the score, a modal asks first and offers "don't ask again this session". A failed request shows a message at bottom-right with a **Copy** button; dismiss it with the **x**. In the prompt bar, the **Up** and **Down** arrows cycle through previous prompts.

Generating from scratch can take anywhere from a few seconds to about a minute. On the free tier, a from-scratch request writes only a few bars (about four), so build longer pieces by asking for more: `add 8 more bars`, `continue`. Whole-piece generation is a Pro feature.

title: Editing notes by hand
body:
## Editing notes by hand

Every change made here is a manual edit, separate from the chat. Click a note or rest to select it; a floating menu opens above it. Press **Esc** to clear the selection.

To change pitch, press **Arrow Up/Down** to move one step or **Shift+Arrow Up/Down** to move an octave. Dragging a notehead vertically does the same, with **Shift** held for octaves. Drag a notehead horizontally to reorder it, even across a barline.

To insert a note, click an empty spot on the staff at the pitch height and beat wanted. The toolbar note picker sets the duration and accidental for placed notes.

Set the selected note's duration with the number keys (matching buttons sit in the floating menu):

| Key | Duration |
| --- | --- |
| **1** | 32nd |
| **2** | 16th |
| **3** | eighth |
| **4** | quarter |
| **5** | half |
| **6** | whole |

Press **.** to toggle a dot. For accidentals, press **=** (sharp), **-** (flat), or **0** (natural).

Build chords by pressing **c** or clicking **+Chord**, then stack pitches with **Shift+A** through **Shift+G**. **Shift+click** an empty spot adds a pitch there; **Alt+click** forces a new note instead.

Press **Shift+I** for tie options. Press **Delete** or **Backspace** to remove the selection.

Undo and redo with **Cmd/Ctrl+Z** and **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z**; each manual edit and each AI generation is one step. The toolbar **Reset** button discards manual edits back to the last AI version.

title: Articulation & expression
body:
## Articulation & expression

Select a note, and the floating menu groups marks into submenus: **Articulation**, **Expression**, **Text**, **Lines**, and **Structure**. Most marks also carry a Shift+letter shortcut that fires while a note is selected.

**Articulation** toggles directly on the note: staccato, accent, tenuto, marcato, fermata, breath mark, caesura, up-bow, and down-bow. Bowing marks apply to string parts.

Expression covers the rest of the per-note vocabulary:

| Submenu | Key | Adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamics | **Shift+D** | `p`, `mf`, `f`, `ff`, `sfz`, niente, `sub. p` |
| Ornaments | **Shift+O** | trill, mordent, turn, arpeggio, slide, tremolo slashes (1-5), jazz inflections |
| Performance technique | **Shift+P** | pizzicato, arco, col legno, sul ponticello, mute on/off, snap pizzicato |
| Fingering | **Shift+F** | piano 1-5, guitar p-c, string or organ forms |
| Grace notes | **Shift+R** | acciaccatura, multi-note runs, grace chords |
| Lyrics | **Shift+V** | syllables with verse numbers; hyphens; extender lines |
| Chord symbol | **Shift+H** | `C`, `Cmaj7`, `F#m7b5`, `C/E`, modal labels |
| Annotation | **Shift+T** | plain, italic, or bold text; rehearsal mark; tempo or expression mark |

Spans run from the selected note to an end note. The span marks are hairpin (**Shift+W**); slur (**Shift+S**); accel./rit. (**Shift+L**); 8va/8vb (**Shift+U**); glissando (**Shift+G**); trill line (**Shift+Z**); tremolo between notes (**Shift+X**).

Rests don't take lyrics; they also reject grace notes and fingerings. Span popovers need a real note.

title: Structure & layout
body:
## Structure & layout

Work on the score above the level of single notes: whole measures, repeats, and global setup.

**Measures.** **Cmd/Ctrl+click** a bar to select it, then **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+click** another bar to extend the selection into a range. Drag a selected range to move it. **Cmd/Ctrl+D** duplicates it and drops the copy right after. **Shift+Delete** removes the selection, always through a confirmation dialog. **+Measure** in the toolbar adds an empty bar.

**Barlines and repeats.** **Shift+J** sets the barline at a measure: double, final, repeat, invisible, plus pickup and final-partial bars. Voltas (**Shift+K**) bracket the 1st and 2nd endings of a repeat. Jump markers (**Shift+Y**) place the navigation marks D.C., D.S., al Coda, and Fine.

**Mid-piece changes.** A marker (**Shift+M**) changes the key, meter, tempo, or clef at a chosen measure, or adds a metric modulation.

**Global setup.** The toolbar **Setup** submenu holds the score-wide controls: key signature, meter (4/4, 3/4, 6/8, or a custom value), tempo in BPM, and a clef per staff. It also switches between a single staff and a grand staff, and adds voices for polyphony (up to four per staff, V1 to V4). Click a voice chip to switch voices, or its **x** to remove one. The score-info button edits the title, composer, and other score details.

title: The command palette
body:
## The command palette

The command palette runs any editor action from one searchable list. Open it with **Cmd+K** (Mac) or **Ctrl+K** (Windows/Linux) from anywhere in the editor; **Esc** closes it.

Type to fuzzy-search command names. Every word typed must match, so narrowing terms like `add slur` trims the list fast. **Arrow Up** and **Arrow Down** move the highlight, and **Enter** or a click runs the highlighted command. When a command also has a direct keyboard shortcut, the palette shows that shortcut on the right of its row.

Commands sit in groups:

- **Score**: score info
- **Markers**: mid-piece key, meter, tempo, and clef
- **Event**: dynamics, chord symbols, lyrics, ties, fingerings, ornaments, techniques, grace notes, annotations
- **Span**: hairpins, slurs, tempo and octave spans, glissando, trill line, tremolo
- **Measure**: barlines, voltas, jump markers, delete
- **View**: keyboard shortcuts, chord palette, chat panel, follow playback
- **Insert**: note durations and accidentals

Many commands need a selection. Selection-gated commands only appear when a note or measure is selected, and that availability is fixed the moment the palette opens. Select first, then open it.

title: Playback
body:
## Playback

The transport bar plays the score with a synthesized soundfont and shows the tempo, the current measure number, and elapsed and total time.

Press the **play/pause** button or the **Space** bar to start and stop, as long as focus isn't in a text field. The **restart** button or the **Home** key returns to the beginning; **Shift+click** the restart button to play immediately from the top.

To seek, click or drag the scrubber. With the scrubber focused, these keys move the playhead:

| Key | Moves |
| --- | --- |
| **Left** / **Right** | one measure |
| **Shift+Left** / **Shift+Right** | one beat |
| **Home** / **End** | start or end |

The **repeat** button loops the score, restarting it at the end, and highlights when on.

Drag the **volume** slider to set the level, or use the **mute** button to silence playback.

The transport overflow menu (**...**) has a **Follow score** option that keeps the playing note in view.

title: Import & export
body:
## Import & export

sheet-llm reads scores from common formats and writes them back out for playback, printing, and other notation apps.

The **Import** button sits in the header. It accepts MusicXML, MIDI, ABC text, and JSON, plus three built-in samples: Twinkle Twinkle, Greensleeves, Bach Minuet. Drag in a file or paste ABC or JSON text. Selecting a built-in sample works too. Each import starts a new session.

MusicXML import takes uncompressed `.xml` or `.musicxml` files only. Compressed `.mxl` files are rejected with a message to export uncompressed first. The import keeps key, meter, clef, staves, notes, rests, chords, accidentals, ties, tuplets, tempo, and metadata. A few advanced details are dropped.

Export uses the buttons below the score:

- **Download MIDI** and **Download PDF** match the on-screen rendering.
- **Download MusicXML** writes a full-fidelity file that opens in the major notation editors: MuseScore, Sibelius, Finale.

The **Download MusicXML** button appears once the score is stable, meaning there's no pending AI proposal.

title: Sessions, settings & tips
body:
## Sessions, settings & tips

The left sidebar holds saved sessions, and a few preferences and shortcuts shape day-to-day work. Most settings stick between visits.

Click a session row to switch to it, double-click its title to rename, or hover a row and click the **x** to delete it. To start fresh, use **Blank score** in the header for a single treble-clef staff in 4/4. **New from prompt** instead clears to a new score built from a text request. Typing a prompt on the empty start screen also opens a session.

Sessions survive a lost browser cookie through a recovery token kept in the browser. Restore runs automatically on the next visit, though it can't recover if local data has been cleared.

A few controls:

- **Sun/Moon** toggle (top-right): switch light and dark; the choice is remembered.
- **Cmd/Ctrl+/**: show or hide chat history on narrow screens. On wide screens the panel stays visible.
- Zoom: hold **Cmd/Ctrl** and scroll, or pinch on a trackpad. The zoom bar at the top-left does the same. Steps run from 25% to 200%.

Generating from scratch can take up to about a minute, and on the free tier each from-scratch request writes only a few bars. One rough edge: the playback cursor can drift slightly after a seek.
